doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Hands, mind, mood, and teaching kids to improvise
summary: Lamb discusses how improvising happens quickly, how he teaches kids, and how nerves vanish once he starts playing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Wow. That’s almost like a physics kind of question, because it’s so — I don’t know it happens so fast, it just happens — you know the response of the notes cause the next thing to happen so quickly man. And that’s the beauty of it. You know it isn’t magic. I think everybody can do it. You know I teach some kids at this gifted school I teach at once a week and you know they don’t have any knowledge of the past of music or whatever. Okay what’s the name of that? You have to name it. That was actually a question I use sometimes is where do you get your titles from. Do you think your mood affects the way that you would improvise?

That’s a good question. The only way I can think of to answer that is like going to do a concert and I’m nervous. Oh man I don’t feel connected, I don’t feel grounded, you know and I hope I’m going to be able to play. I do these little things, and right up to the point of the gig. And then, “Ladies and gentlemen” blah-blah and then you go out and it’s all gone again. It’s all like I knew you’d be there.
Why did you have to wait so long?
Yeah, but you know, so whatever that process is. So as far as the mood I think as soon as I start playing there’s some switch that goes off. You know it, you know that feeling.
